title: The Navy ship that vanished with about 300 people and sent no call for help
hook: A huge US Navy ship vanished with about three hundred people and never called for help.
summary: In 1918 the USS Cyclops, a huge Navy ship, disappeared after leaving Barbados with about 300 people, leaving no wreckage, and her two sister ships vanished the same way in 1941.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Naval History and Heritage Command: USS Cyclops (AC-4), a collier, left Barbados on 4 March 1918 for Baltimore and was lost with about 300 people aboard; no distress call and no wreckage were found.
Naval History and Heritage Command: Cyclops carried a heavy load of manganese ore and had a damaged engine; it is the largest non-combat loss of life in US Naval history.
Naval History and Heritage Command: sister ships USS Proteus and USS Nereus disappeared in late 1941 on the Atlantic route, carrying heavy ore.

lines.text: In March nineteen eighteen, the USS Cyclops left Barbados for Baltimore.
She carried heavy ore, and one engine was damaged.
She never arrived. No wreckage, no bodies, no radio message.
The Navy searched for months and found nothing.
Maybe the overloaded ship broke apart. Nobody knows.
Then in nineteen forty-one, her two sister ships vanished on the same route.
To this day, nobody knows why.

post.caption:
The Cyclops is the biggest non-combat loss of life in US Navy history, and no one has found a trace.
